title: Quantile Regression for Censored Time-to-Event Data with a Cure Fraction
text: loading relevant R packages, cure quantile regression model can fit using curequantile function. coef() function extracts parameter estimates specific quantile tau. , gamma_est contains incidence parameter estimates, beta_est contains latency parameter estimates specified quantile, tau. Finally, eta_est gives conditional probabilities susceptible, therefore length equal number rows input data frame. Alternatively, print() prints coefficients user-specified quantile tau console. summary() function returns parameter estimates, bootstrap standard error estimates, Z-test, p-value, bootstrap confidence interval incidence covariates latency covariates indicated quantile, tau. plot() function produces plot quantile estimate corresponding confidence interval covariate range user-specified quantiles tau. functions designed handle resulting model object include: dim(), formula(), logLik(), nobs(), predict().
code: library(curequantile) library(survival) library(maxLik) #> Loading required package: miscTools #>  #> Please cite the 'maxLik' package as: #> Henningsen, Arne and Toomet, Ott (2011). maxLik: A package for maximum likelihood estimation in R. Computational Statistics 26(3), 443-458. DOI 10.1007/s00180-010-0217-1. #>  #> If you have questions, suggestions, or comments regarding the 'maxLik' package, please use its GitHub page and the issues there: #> https://github.com/arne-henningsen/maxLik data("breast_data") fit_breast <- curequantile(Surv(log(Time), Delta) ~ Age + Size,   data = breast_data, subset = 1:200) coefficients <- coef(fit_breast, tau = 0.25) names(coefficients) #> [1] "gamma_est" "eta_est"   "beta_est" coefficients$gamma_est #> (Intercept)         Age        Size  #> -4.41474759  0.03760906  0.03203235
